section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch — Special Education
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A pupil who can read and understand content well but produces illegible handwriting, struggles with spelling and letter-spacing, and finds the physical act of writing exhausting and slow, most likely has:
explanation: Dysgraphia specifically impairs written expression (handwriting, spelling, organising thoughts on paper) despite normal reading comprehension — distinct from dyslexia (reading), dyscalculia (mathematics), or dyspraxia (motor coordination more broadly).

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch — Special Education
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A pupil who struggles specifically with number concepts, arithmetic operations and understanding quantities, despite normal ability in reading, likely has:
explanation: Dyscalculia specifically affects mathematical understanding; dyslexia affects reading; dysgraphia affects handwriting/written expression; aphasia is a language-production/comprehension impairment usually from brain injury.
